name: French Algeria
definition: Published 1896 total for the three Algerian departments. Includes the army. The exact enumeration day and local perimeter changes before 1901 have not been verified. The municipal count is separately reported. The army coverage prevents direct interpolation against the 1901 total.

name: French Algeria
definition: Initial total for the three Algerian departments before the new Saharan annexes were included. The later census comparison records that the army was omitted. The final old-scope total exceeds this publication by 225 people.

name: French Algeria
locator: Printed pp. 181–182, total, municipal count and split by territory.
method: published revised quinquennial census total on the older administrative scope
definition: Civil territory plus the older territory of command. The six new Saharan annexes are excluded. The army was not enumerated. The total includes 16,331 people counted separately from the municipal population, including boarding students, religious communities, hospital patients and prisoners. The three departmental totals and the territorial split independently sum to the published total. The historical administrative boundary has not been reconciled to the opening map.

name: French Algeria with six new Saharan annexes
locator: Printed p. 24, 1901 comparison and note 2. Official register, preface and printed pp. 208–213.
method: published revised census total with appended territory returns
definition: Revised 1901 census series including six annexes of the Aïn-Sefra subdivision. These are Béni-Abbès, Djenan-ed-Dar, Zousfana, In-Salah, Timimoun and Touat. The official appendix records 61,919 under the situation on 1 November 1902. The remaining 4,739,556 is the revised old-scope count of 21 March 1901. The composite is assigned to the source’s 1901 census series. The army was omitted from that census.
